output.summary: The backlog growth is mostly self-inflicted by the quota's incentives. First-contact demand rose only 4%. Splits (240 to 3,710), duplicates (410 to 2,770) and reopens (6% to 23%) account for the surge. The exempt Billing-Compliance pod stayed flat, and Team C improved its reopen rate when it stopped counting reopened closes. The reopen rate is not a configuration artifact, and headcount and hours were flat. Payroll adds only about 380 first-contact tickets a month. Engineering bug backlog may contribute to aged complex tickets, but this is unquantified. Raising the quota is harmful, and hiring 12 permanent agents is premature. Replace the quota with quality measures and classify the aged tickets.
